lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Our languages are different, but our hearts are the same. Today, we leave the Rainbow Bridge and walk toward the light far away. We walk and walk across the clouds. Look! There is a rocky island in a sea of clouds. On the island, there is a tall white lighthouse. This is the Lighthouse of Ideas! At the door, an old dog wags his tail. His name is Anchor. Then a kind old pelican comes out. He wears a captain's hat. He is Captain Pell, the keeper of the lighthouse. He says, Welcome to the Lighthouse of Ideas! We climb the stairs to the top. Captain Pell points at the big lamp. He says, This light shines when people share ideas. Say it with me. This light shines when people share ideas. Wonderful! But the light is very weak. Kiko asks, Why is the light so weak? Captain Pell answers, Nobody shares ideas now. Some animals argue loudly. Some animals say nothing at all. Let's read the old sign on the wall. "The Lighthouse of Ideas. This lamp shines when people share ideas and listen to each other. Around the lamp, there are six lenses. Kind words and good ideas light the lenses, one by one. When all six lenses shine, the light reaches far across the sea. Then little boats can find their way home, even on dark and foggy nights. Please speak kindly, listen carefully, and share your ideas. From Captain Pell, Keeper of the Light." How many lenses are there? Six. What happens when all six lenses shine? The light reaches far across the sea. Now, phonics. Today's word part is spect. Spect means look or see. Respect. You look again and think someone is important. Inspect. You look into something carefully. Spectator. A person watching a game. Suspect. You think someone did something wrong. Let's help Captain Pell light the lamp!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, This light shines when people share ideas. Today, we sit by the warm stove in the lighthouse kitchen. Anchor sleeps on his soft blanket. Captain Pell smiles and asks, Which animal makes a good pet? Haru looks at Anchor and says, I think dogs are great pets because they're loyal. Say it with me. I think dogs are great pets because they're loyal. Great job! The word loyal（ちゅうじつ） means you stay with your friend and never leave. First, say your opinion with I think. Then, say because and give your reason. Captain Pell asks, Why do you think so? Kiko says, Because they're friendly. Then Riko says, I think cats are great pets because they're calm. Birimo says, I think a cake is a great pet because it's sweet! Everyone laughs. A cake can't be a pet, Birimo! Look! The light flickers a little. Let's read the Pet Talk board in the kitchen. "Pet Talk Board. Which animal makes a good pet? Haru: I think dogs are great pets because they're loyal. Riko: I think cats are great pets because they're calm and clean. Kiko: I think rabbits are great pets because they're soft and gentle. Birimo: I think goldfish are great pets because they're fun to watch. Captain Pell: I think all pets are great because they make us happy. Please write your idea on a card, too! Every idea is welcome here." Why does Riko like cats? Because they're calm and clean. What does Captain Pell think? All pets are great. Now, phonics. Spect means look. Inspector. A person checking things carefully. Respectful. You show respect to others. Spectacular. Wonderful to look at, like fireworks! Perspective. The way you see things. Let's share our ideas about pets!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think dogs are great pets because they're loyal. Today, Captain Pell teaches us a new trick. He says, An opinion is good. An opinion with an example is even stronger. Every evening, Captain Pell goes down to the beach. And every evening, Anchor waits for him at the door. Captain Pell says, I think dogs are loyal. For example, my dog waits for me every day. Say it with me. For example, my dog waits for me every day. Wonderful! Then Birimo puts on a paper captain's hat. He says, I'm playing Captain Pell! For example, my dog waits for me every day. Anchor wags his tail. Riko tries, too. Cats are clean. For example, they wash their faces every day. Captain Pell says, That's a great example! Let's read a page in Captain Pell's notebook. "How to Make Your Opinion Strong. Step one: Say your opinion. I think penguins are amazing. Step two: Give a reason. Because they're great swimmers. Step three: Give an example. For example, they can swim very fast and dive deep for fish. An example is like a picture. It helps your friends see your idea. Without an example, your idea is like a dark room. With an example, the room gets bright! Try it with your favorite animal today!" What is step three? Give an example. Why is an example like a picture? It helps your friends see your idea. Now, phonics. Spect means look. Inspection. A careful look at something. The lighthouse has an inspection every year. Disrespect. Dis means not. Disrespect means not showing respect. Spectrum. A band of many colors, like a rainbow. Do you remember the Rainbow Bridge? Let's make our opinions strong with examples!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, For example, my dog waits for me every day. Today, more island animals come to the lighthouse. They sit on the rocks and listen. Captain Pell asks, Which is better, cats or dogs? Kiko asks Riko, Why do you like cats? Riko says, I have two reasons. One reason is that cats are quiet. Another reason is that they're easy to care for. Say it with me. One reason is that cats are quiet. Another reason is that they're easy to care for. Excellent! Two reasons make your opinion strong. Then Haru says, Dogs are great, too. One reason is that they love to play. Captain Pell nods and says, Both ideas are good. Cats and dogs are both wonderful. The animals clap their wings and paws. The light shines a little more. Let's read Riko's and Haru's posts on the lighthouse board. "Riko: I think cats are great pets. One reason is that cats are quiet. They don't bark at night. Another reason is that they're easy to care for. You don't need to walk them. Haru: I think dogs are great pets. One reason is that they love to play. We can run in the park together. Another reason is that dogs are loyal. They always stay with you. Captain Pell: Thank you, Riko and Haru. Both ideas are good, and both pets are wonderful!" Why are cats easy to care for? You don't need to walk them. What can Haru do with a dog? Run in the park together. Now, phonics. Spect means look. Spectacles. Another word for glasses. Captain Pell wears round spectacles to read. Aspect. One side of something. A good aspect of cats is their quiet voice. Respectable. People respect it. A respectable captain is honest and kind. Use two reasons, and your ideas will shine!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, One reason is that cats are quiet. Another reason is that they're easy to care for. Today, we climb to the lamp room. Captain Pell says, Please share your ideas. Each idea makes the light stronger. Kiko goes first. I think reading is fun. One reason is that books take us to new places. For example, I visited a dragon island in a story. Say it with me. I think reading is fun. One reason is that books take us to new places. For example, I visited a dragon island in a story. Wonderful! The light gets brighter! Captain Pell says, Thank you for sharing your idea! Then he asks Riko, What do you think is fun? Riko says, I think drawing is fun. One reason is that I can draw my dreams. Birimo says, I think baking is fun. For example, I baked a giant cake. Then I ate it all! Suddenly, one lens begins to shine. The first lens is lit! Let's read Captain Pell's lighthouse log. "Lighthouse Log, Day Five. Today, my young friends shared their ideas in the lamp room. Each friend gave an opinion, a reason, and an example. Kiko talked about books. Riko talked about drawing. Birimo talked about cake, of course. With every idea, the lamp grew brighter. Tonight, the first lens is shining. Five more lenses are waiting. I can see a little boat far away. It's coming home safely. Anchor and I are very happy tonight." How many lenses are shining now? One. What did Birimo talk about? Cake, of course! Now, phonics. Let's review spect. Respect. Look again and value someone. Perspective. Your way of seeing things. Spectator. A person watching. Inspect. Look into something carefully. Great work, everyone! See you next time!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think reading is fun. One reason is that books take us to new places. For example, I visited a dragon island in a story. Today, Captain Pell opens a round wooden door. Wow! It's the lighthouse library! There are books about the sea, the stars, and faraway islands. Kiko says, Reading is fun! Haru says, I agree with you. Reading is fun. Say it with me. I agree with you. Reading is fun. Great! When you have the same idea as your friend, say, I agree with you. Riko says, I think books are better at night. Do you agree with me? Birimo says, Yes, I do. Books and snacks are better at night! Kiko finds a big blue book and says, Me too! I love stories about the sea. Captain Pell laughs. He says, When friends agree, they still listen. They say why. Let's read the poster on the library door. "Book Talk Time in the Lighthouse Library. Every Friday evening, bring your favorite book. Tell your friends about it. Say why you like it. Listen when your friends talk. Say, I agree with you, when you have the same idea. Ask a question when you want to know more. You can borrow two books at a time. Please bring them back in one week. Snacks are OK, but please keep the books clean! From Captain Pell." When is Book Talk Time? Every Friday evening. Are snacks OK? Yes, but keep the books clean. Now, phonics. Today's new word part is dict. Dict means say. Predict. Pre means before. You say it before it happens. Dictionary. A book of words. Let's look it up in the dictionary! Contradict. Contra means against. You say the opposite. Let's find a good book together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I agree with you. Reading is fun. Today, we hear loud voices outside. Two seagull brothers are on the rocks. Their names are Gus and Gale. Gus shouts, The mountains are more fun! Gale shouts, No! The beach is more fun! They don't listen to each other. Oh no! The light gets weaker. Captain Pell sighs. I say, Let's try a kind way to answer. First, show you heard your friend. Then, give your own idea. Gus tries first. He says, I think the mountains are more fun because we can hike. Gale takes a deep breath. He says, I see your point, but I think the beach is more fun. Say it with me. I see your point, but I think the beach is more fun. Wonderful! Gus is surprised. He says, Oh. Thank you for listening. Captain Pell smiles and says, Let's listen to each other. Let's read Gus and Gale's notes on the lighthouse board. "Gus: I think the mountains are more fun because we can hike and see beautiful views. The air is cool and fresh, too. Gale: I see your point, but I think the beach is more fun. We can swim, build sandcastles, and play in the waves. The sound of the sea is relaxing, and the sand feels warm under our feet. Captain Pell: Both ideas are good. Mountains and beaches are both special places. Thank you for writing kindly!" Why does Gus like the mountains? Because he can hike and see beautiful views. What can Gale do at the beach? Swim, build sandcastles, and play in the waves. Now, phonics. Dict means say. Prediction. A guess about the future. My prediction is rain tomorrow. Dictation. Your teacher says words, and you write them down. Verdict. The final decision. Let's listen first and speak kindly!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I see your point, but I think the beach is more fun. Today, Gus and Gale fly to Kiko. Gus asks, Kiko, the mountains are more fun, right? Gale asks, No, the beach is more fun, right? Kiko thinks and thinks. Both places are nice. She says, I'm not sure about that. Say it with me. I'm not sure about that. Good! We can say this when we can't decide yet. And that's OK. Then Birimo asks, Which is better, cake or ice cream? Haru says, Hmm, it's hard to decide. Riko says, Both are nice. I can't choose. Captain Pell smiles and says, It's OK to take your time. A good thinker doesn't rush. Let's read the Big Question card on the lighthouse wall. "Big Question of the Week: Which is better, a rainy day or a sunny day? Little Crab says, Sunny days are better because I can play on the warm sand. Old Turtle says, Rainy days are better because the rocks are cool and wet. Young Rabbit says, I'm not sure about that. I like sunny days, but rain helps the carrots grow. What do you think? Write your answer below. It's OK to be unsure." Why does Old Turtle like rainy days? Because the rocks are cool and wet. Why is Young Rabbit not sure? Because rain helps the carrots grow. Now, phonics. Dict means say. Predictable. You can say the ending before it happens. This story is very predictable. Unpredictable. Un means not. Island weather is unpredictable! Sunny, then rainy, then sunny again. Dictate. You say words, and a friend writes them down. When you're not sure, it's OK to say so!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I'm not sure about that. Today is a hot, sunny day on the island. Gus and Gale are talking again, but this time they're calm. Gus says, Summer is the best season because we can swim and fly over the sparkling sea. Gale thinks. He likes some of Gus's idea, but not all of it. Gale says, I partly agree. Summer is fun, but it's too hot. Say it with me. I partly agree. Summer is fun, but it's too hot. Fantastic! Partly means a part, not all. First, say the good part. Then, say but and the other part. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I partly agree. Summer is fun, but it's too hot. Today, Captain Pell starts the Agree or Disagree Game! Everybody comes to the beach below the lighthouse. Gus and Gale come, too. Captain Pell reads a sentence. Summer is the best season. If you agree, stand on the left. If you disagree, stand on the right. Then give a reason. Haru stands on the left. He says, I agree because summer vacation is long. Riko stands on the right. She says, I disagree because winter is my favorite season. Say it with me. I disagree because winter is my favorite season. Great! Riko loves skating and hot soup. Gus says, I see your point, Riko. Gale says, Both ideas are good! Nobody shouts. Everyone listens. Then the brothers play too, and they take turns kindly. Suddenly, the second lens begins to shine! Now two lenses are lit! Let's read the game card. "The Agree or Disagree Game. One: Listen to the sentence. Two: Choose a side. Stand on the left if you agree. Stand on the right if you disagree. Three: Say, I agree because, or, I disagree because, and give a reason. Four: Listen to the other side. Five: Clap for every idea. Six: Say thank you to the other team. Remember, there is no wrong side. Every reason is welcome. Kind words make the light shine!" Where do you stand to disagree? On the right. What should you do for every idea? Clap for it. Now, phonics. Let's review dict and spect. Predict. Say before. Contradict. Say against. Respectful. You show respect. Perspective. Your way of seeing things. You're all wonderful players. See you next time!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I disagree because winter is my favorite season. Gus and Gale played the game kindly, and the second lens began to shine. Today, Captain Pell takes us to the round meeting room. There is a big round table in the middle, so everyone can see everyone. Captain Pell says, The island festival is coming soon. What should we make for it? Haru says, I think we should make paper lanterns. Then he turns to Kiko. What do you think, Kiko? Say it with me. What do you think, Kiko? Great job! Say the name at the end, and your friend knows it's her turn. Riko asks, What do you think about paper lanterns? Kiko smiles and says, I think they're beautiful. But a big kite is fun too. Then Kiko asks, How about you, Birimo? Birimo says, I think we should make a giant cake! Everyone laughs. Let's read the notice on the meeting room door. "Island Festival Meeting. Date: Saturday, at ten in the morning. Place: the round meeting room. Topic: What should we make for the festival? Please bring one idea. You can draw it or write it. Every idea is welcome, big or small. At the meeting, we will sit around the round table. Each friend will share one idea, and then we will talk about it. Listen to your friends and ask, What do you think? The festival is next week, so let's decide soon! From Captain Pell" When is the meeting? On Saturday, at ten in the morning. What should you bring? One idea. Now, phonics. When we feel strongly, we make one word loud and long. I really think so. I REALLY think so. I totally agree with you. I TOTALLY agree with you. This is so much fun. This is SO much fun. I love this idea. I LOVE this idea. Now it's your turn. What do you think? Let's share our ideas!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What do you think, Kiko? We have three ideas for the festival: lanterns, a kite, and a giant cake. Today, we talk about festival food. Captain Pell says, Riko, will you be the chair today? The chair leads the meeting. Riko says, OK! Then Gus and Gale fly in. Gus shouts, Fish sandwiches! Gale shouts, No, rice balls! They both talk at the same time. Nobody can hear anything. Riko stands up and says, Let's hear from everyone. Say it with me. Let's hear from everyone. Wonderful! Then Riko asks, Who wants to go first? Gus says, I do! Riko gives him a big white shell. Only the speaker holds the shell. When Gus finishes, Riko says, Thank you, Gus. Next, Gale, please. Gale holds the shell and speaks. Nobody shouts now. The lamp glows a little warmer. Let's read Captain Pell's card for the chair. "How to Be a Good Chair. One: Say the topic clearly. Two: Ask, Who wants to go first? Three: Give everyone a turn, and don't forget quiet friends. Four: Say thank you after each speaker. Five: Keep your own idea for the end. A good chair listens more and talks less. Then everyone feels safe to share. Remember, the chair is not the boss. The chair is a helper for the whole group. Smile, speak slowly, and enjoy the meeting!" Who should the chair not forget? Quiet friends. When does the chair share her own idea? At the end. Now, phonics. Make the strong word loud and a little long. We definitely need a break. We DEFINITELY need a break. I strongly believe it. I STRONGLY believe it. That's absolutely true. That's ABSOLUTELY true. I never said that. I NEVER said that. Great job, chairs! Next time, let's hear from everyone again!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Let's hear from everyone. Riko was a great chair, and Gus and Gale took turns with the white shell. Today, the meeting goes on. The topic is decorations for the festival. Everyone talks fast. Kiko has an idea, but she can't find a chance to speak. So she raises her hand and says, Can I say something? Say it with me. Can I say something? Very good! Riko smiles and says, Sure, go ahead. Kiko says, Let's put lanterns on the little boats. Then the boats can see each other at night. Everyone claps. Then Gale raises his wing. Can I add one more thing? Riko says, Sure, go ahead. Gale says, Seagulls can hang lanterns on the tall rocks. Captain Pell nods, and Anchor wags his tail. Say it with me. Sure, go ahead. Let's read the poster on the wall of the round room. "Round Room Rules. Raise your hand or your wing. Wait for a short pause. Then say, Can I say something? Please don't speak while a friend is speaking. Listen to the end, and then add your idea. Short ideas and long ideas are both OK. Are you shy? You can write your idea on a card. Captain Pell will read it for you. Every voice is important here. When we take turns, the lamp shines brighter, and the little boats can find their way." What can you say after a pause? Can I say something? What can shy friends do? They can write their idea on a card. Now, phonics. Say the strong word loud and long. I completely understand. I COMPLETELY understand. Reading is very important. Reading is VERY important. I do agree with you. I DO agree with you. That's exactly my point. That's EXACTLY my point. Raise your hand and join in!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Can I say something? Kiko joined in, and her lantern idea was a big hit. Today, we have one more thing to decide. After the festival, there is a picnic. Where should we go? There are three ideas: the park, the beach, and the lighthouse garden. Everyone talks and talks. Captain Pell says, We need to decide. Riko says, Let's vote. Raise your hand if you like the park. Six hands and wings go up. Raise your hand if you like the beach. Three go up. Captain Pell raises his wing for the garden. Riko counts and says, Most people chose the park. It's decided! Say it with me. Let's vote. Most people chose the park. Super! Everyone shouts, Hooray! Gus wanted the beach, but he smiles and says, OK! The park is fine. Maybe the beach next time. Captain Pell says, That's a kind answer, Gus. Voting is a good way to decide, and a kind answer makes it even better. Let's read the vote board. "Picnic Vote Results. The park: six votes. The beach: three votes. The lighthouse garden: one vote. Total: ten votes. Most people chose the park! The picnic is on Sunday after the festival. Please bring a hat and a water bottle. Gus and Gale will bring the music. Birimo will bring a cake, of course. Thank you for voting, everyone. Your idea was not chosen? That's OK. We can try it next time. See you at the park!" How many votes did the beach get? Three. What should you bring? A hat and a water bottle. Now, phonics. Make the strong word loud and long. It was such a good game. It was SUCH a good game. We really should try. We REALLY should try. I always keep my promises. I ALWAYS keep my promises. You are so right. You are SO right. Let's vote and decide together!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Let's vote. Most people chose the park. Today, I have a plan. At school, you may have class meetings, too. Let's practice here! Haru is the chair this time. He stands up and says, Today's topic is our school trip. What do you think? Say it with me. Today's topic is our school trip. What do you think? Excellent! Riko says, I'd like to go to the aquarium because I love sea animals. Haru says, Let's hear from Kiko. Kiko says, I think the science museum is better. We can try fun experiments. Then Birimo raises his hand. Can I say something? Haru says, Sure, go ahead. Birimo says, The farm! They have fresh ice cream! Everyone laughs. Then Haru says, Let's vote. Everyone votes, and Haru says, Most people chose the aquarium. Suddenly, the third lens begins to shine! Captain Pell says, Wonderful! You asked, you listened, and you decided together. Let's read Kiko's meeting notes. "Class Meeting Notes. Topic: our school trip. Chair: Haru. Ideas: the aquarium, the science museum, and the farm. Riko likes the aquarium because she loves sea animals. Kiko likes the science museum because of the experiments. Birimo likes the farm because of the ice cream. Vote: the aquarium, five. The science museum, three. The farm, two. Decision: the aquarium. Everyone listened to each other, and nobody shouted. Birimo was a little sad about the ice cream, but he clapped for the aquarium. Next time, the science museum!" Who was the chair? Haru. Why does Kiko like the science museum? Because of the experiments. Now, phonics. I really think so. I REALLY think so. I do agree with you. I DO agree with you. Listen, dictionary. Dict means say. Now, spectator. Spect means look. Three lenses are shining now. Great teamwork, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Today's topic is our school trip. What do you think? Three lenses are shining now! Today, we climb the stairs to the lamp room at the top. Gale looks at the new lens and says, Wow, it's so cool! Birimo touches it. Hmm, it isn't cold. It's warm! Kiko asks Gale, What do you mean by "cool"? Say it with me. What do you mean by "cool"? Nice! Gale laughs. Cool can mean a little cold. But here, it means great. Birimo says, Oh, it means great! Gale says, Right. Then Captain Pell says, Now, let's go down to the galley for some tea. Haru asks, What does galley mean? Captain Pell says, It means a kitchen on a ship. My lighthouse is like a big ship! When you don't know a word, just ask. It isn't rude. It helps everyone understand. Let's read the list on the galley wall. "Captain Pell's Sailor Words. Galley means a kitchen on a ship. Deck means the floor of a ship. Ahoy means hello, and it is fun to shout! Aye aye means yes, I understand. Stern means the back of a ship. Shipshape means neat and clean. Sailors use these words every day. Some of them sound strange, but they are easy to learn. Ask me about any word, any time. I love questions!" What does deck mean? The floor of a ship. How do sailors say hello? Ahoy! Now, phonics. In fast speech, can is short and weak. It sounds like kun. I can help you. We can do it together. Can you say that again? You can sit here. When you hear a new word, ask, What do you mean? Have fun with new words!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, What do you mean by "cool"? Now we know. It means great! Today, we are in the galley. Remember, a galley is a kitchen on a ship. Captain Pell pours some tea and says, Tomorrow is the festival. The sky is clear in the morning, but thick fog comes after lunch. Haru thinks for a moment. Then he says, So you mean we should start early? Say it with me. So you mean we should start early? Great! Captain Pell says, Yes, exactly. Haru says, Got it! When you say, So you mean, you say the idea in your own words. Then you can check it. Riko asks, So you mean we should start at five in the morning? Captain Pell laughs. Not quite. I mean we should finish before lunch. Seven o'clock is fine. Birimo asks, So you mean breakfast comes first? Captain Pell says, Yes, exactly! Let's read Captain Pell's plan for tomorrow. "Festival Day Plan. Seven o'clock: breakfast in the galley. Eight o'clock: hang the lanterns on the boats. Nine o'clock: Gus and Gale put flags on the rocks. Ten o'clock: practice the festival songs. Eleven thirty: everything is ready! After lunch, the fog comes, so please stay inside and rest. In the evening, the fog goes away, and the festival begins. Lanterns on: six o'clock. Songs and dancing: seven o'clock. Please bring a jacket, because the night air is chilly. Don't be late!" What time is breakfast? Seven o'clock. When does the festival begin? In the evening. Now, phonics. In fast speech, to is short and weak. It sounds like tuh. I want to go. Let's talk to Kiko. I'd like to say something. It's time to decide. So you mean you're ready? Let's go!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, So you mean we should start early? So today, we get up early. It's festival morning! Everyone is busy at the lighthouse. Gus flies down and says, Seagulls are the best helpers! Riko asks, Could you give me an example? Say it with me. Could you give me an example? Well done! Gus says, Sure. For example, we can carry flags to the rocks. Riko says, That's a great example. Thank you! An example makes your idea clear. Your friend can picture it. Then Birimo says, I'm a great helper too! Haru asks, Could you give me an example? Birimo says, For example, I can taste the cake. Everyone laughs. But then Birimo helps hang the lanterns too. Good job, Birimo! Let's read two posts on the helper board. Do they have the same idea? "Gus: In my opinion, seagulls are the best helpers. For example, we can fly high and put flags on the tall rocks. Nobody else can do that! Kiko: I think small helpers are important too. For example, Anchor is old and slow, but he carries the lantern basket in his mouth. He never drops it. Haru helps with the songs, Riko paints the flags, and Captain Pell watches over everyone. Big or small, fast or slow, every helper is special!" What can seagulls do? They can fly high and put flags on the rocks. What does Anchor carry? The lantern basket. Do Gus and Kiko have the same idea? Not quite. Both ideas are good! Now, phonics. In fast speech, for is short and weak. It sounds like fur. This is for you. Thanks for waiting. Wait for me. It's good for everyone. Could you give me an example of a good helper? Think about it, and have a wonderful festival day!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Could you give me an example? Now it's festival night! Lanterns glow on the little boats, and the sea looks like a sky full of stars. Captain Pell brings out a wooden box. He says, This is the Question Box. The island animals put their questions in it. Kiko picks a card and reads it to Haru. What is the most important thing in a meeting? Haru says, That's a good question. Let me think. Say it with me. That's a good question. Let me think. Perfect! It's OK to take time. A good answer needs a little thinking. After a moment, Haru says, I'm not sure, but I think listening is the most important. Captain Pell nods. Then Riko picks a card for Birimo. Why do boats need a lighthouse? Birimo says, Hmm, give me a second. Then he says, Because the sea is very dark at night! Good answer, Birimo! Let's read some cards from the Question Box. "Question one: Why do boats need a lighthouse? From a little crab. Question two: Is it better to talk first or listen first? From Gale. Question three: Which is more fun, the festival or the picnic? From Gus. Question four: Can Anchor come to the picnic too? He is old, but he loves short walks. From Captain Pell. Please answer with your opinion and a reason! There are no wrong answers in this box. Take your time and think. You can also ask a friend for help. Thank you for your wonderful questions!" Who asked about the festival and the picnic? Gus. What does Anchor love? Short walks. Now, phonics. In fast speech, and is short and weak. It sounds like un. Come and see. Let's stop and think. Kiko and Riko agree. I like black and white. When a question is hard, smile and say, Let me think. You can do it!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, That's a good question. Let me think. The festival was wonderful! Today, it's a quiet morning, and we interview Captain Pell about lighthouse life. Anchor sleeps by his feet. Kiko asks, What's the best part of your job? Captain Pell says, Seeing the boats come home safely. Haru asks, Why do you think so? Captain Pell says, Because families wait for them. Riko asks, Can you tell me more? Say it with me. Why do you think so? Can you tell me more? Great! These are follow-up questions. They help people say more. Captain Pell tells a story. One foggy night long ago, a little boat could not find the island. I rang the bell all night, and Anchor barked and barked. Kiko says, That's interesting! What happened next? Captain Pell smiles. In the morning, the boat came home, and the family gave Anchor a big bone. Suddenly, the fourth lens begins to shine! Let's read Riko's interview card. "Interview with Captain Pell. Job: lighthouse keeper for forty years. Best part of the job: seeing the boats come home safely. Hard part: cleaning the big lamp every day. Favorite food: fish soup. Best friend: Anchor. He waits at the door for me every day. Advice for us: Share your ideas, and listen to others. Then the light gets brighter. Message for young keepers: A lighthouse is like a good friend. It is always there for the boats, and it never gives up. Thank you for the interview!" How long has he been a keeper? For forty years. What is the hard part of his job? Cleaning the big lamp every day. Now, phonics. Can you say that again? Can is weak. It's time to decide. To is weak. That's absolutely true. That's ABSOLUTELY true. Say it, predict. Pre means before, and dict means say. Four lenses are shining now. You are great interviewers!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Why do you think so? Can you tell me more? Today, Captain Pell takes us up a narrow staircase. Look at the lamp! Four lenses are shining now. Only two lenses are still dark. At the top of the stairs, there is a small, busy room. It's the newsroom! A young puffin flies in with a pencil behind her ear. Her name is Pip. She is a reporter, and she makes The Lighthouse News. Pip says, A good newspaper needs facts. A fact（じじつ） is true, and we can check it. An opinion is an idea or a feeling. Other people can feel differently. Pip holds up a picture of a sleeping cat. "Cats sleep a lot" is a fact. Say it with me. "Cats sleep a lot" is a fact. Great! Then Pip says, "Cats are the cutest animals" is an opinion. Birimo says, Is this a fact or an opinion? Birimos are the cutest! Pip laughs. It's an opinion, Birimo! Let's read Pip's news story. "The Lighthouse News, Page Two. Captain Pell has lived in the lighthouse for forty years. The lighthouse has six lenses, and four of them are shining now. Anchor, the captain's dog, waits at the door for him every day. In my opinion, Anchor is the sweetest dog on the island. Last night, three little boats came home safely because of the light. I think the light is the most beautiful thing in the sea of clouds. By Pip, Reporter" How many lenses are shining? Four. Anchor is the sweetest dog on the island. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. The lighthouse has six lenses. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. We can count them! Now, phonics. Possible. Visible. Reasonable. Acceptable. Reason plus able makes reasonable. Accept plus able makes acceptable. Poss and vis are not words by themselves, so they usually take ible. Let's find more facts, reporters!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, "Cats sleep a lot" is a fact. Today, Pip has a question for the island. The newsroom door is old and gray. What color should we paint it? Pip makes a poll for The Lighthouse News. Kiko thinks for a moment. Then she speaks softly. It's just my opinion, but I think green is the best color. Say it with me. It's just my opinion, but I think green is the best color. Nice! Pip says, Those words make your opinion soft and kind. Other people can still share their ideas. Haru says, I respect your opinion. I like blue. Birimo shouts, Brown is the best color, because it looks like chocolate cake! Riko asks, Is that a fact? Birimo grins. No, it's just my opinion. Let's read two posts from the Readers' Corner. "Readers' Corner. Gus says: It's just my opinion, but blue is the best color for the door. Blue is the color of the sea and the sky. It makes me feel calm. Gale says: I respect my brother's opinion, but I think yellow is the best. Yellow is bright and cheerful, like the morning sun. Little boats can see a yellow door from far away. Both of us love the newsroom, so please vote!" What color does Gale like? Yellow. Blue is the color of the sea and the sky. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Yellow is cheerful. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Gus and Gale don't argue now. They listen to each other. Now, phonics. Terrible. Horrible. These are strong words, so be careful with them in a discussion! Suitable. Suit plus able. Understandable. Understand plus able. Terr and horr are not words by themselves, so they usually take ible. Every color is fine, and every opinion counts!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, It's just my opinion, but I think green is the best color. Today, Birimo runs into the newsroom. Big news! There's a giant cake under the lighthouse! Everyone stops. Riko asks two smart questions. Is that true? Where did you read that? Say it with me. Is that true? Where did you read that? Excellent! Birimo says, I read it on a note at the harbor. Haru says, Let's check it together. Kiko says, Good idea! Pip grabs her notebook. A good reporter always checks the news. So the friends walk down to the harbor and find the note. Then they walk behind the lighthouse. What do they find? Let's read Pip's story. "Rumor Check, by Pip. This week, a funny rumor went around the island. A giant cake is hidden under the lighthouse! I found the first note at the harbor. It said, There is a giant lake behind the lighthouse. Someone mixed up lake and cake! Our team walked behind the lighthouse and checked. There is a small blue lake there. There is no cake. Before you share news, please ask two questions. Is that true? Where did you read that?" Where was the first note? At the harbor. What is behind the lighthouse? A small blue lake. There is a small blue lake behind the lighthouse. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. The team checked it with their own eyes. Birimo looks sad. I think a cake is better than a lake! Haru laughs. I see your point, but a lake is great for little boats. Now, phonics. Incredible. Edible. Edible means you can eat it. Is the lake edible? No, Birimo! Remarkable. Remark plus able. Agreeable. Agree plus able. Incred and ed are not words by themselves, so they usually take ible. Always check the news, friends!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Is that true? Where did you read that? Today, Pip is working on the last page of The Lighthouse News. It's the ad page! A shop at the harbor wants to sell a new toy. It's a spinning top, and it looks like a star. The ad has very big words. Haru reads it and frowns. "This is the best toy ever!" Is it a fact? Say it with me. "This is the best toy ever!" Is it a fact? Good thinking! Riko says, No, we can't check it. Kiko points at another line. "It spins for three minutes." We can check that with a clock. Birimo jumps up. I'm playing the toy seller! Everyone loves it! Haru smiles. Hmm, that's an opinion. Let's read the ad together. "NEW! The Spinning Star! This is the best toy ever! It spins for three minutes. It glows in the dark, so you can play at night. It is light and easy to carry, so you can take it to the beach or the park. It comes in five colors. Everyone loves it! You will be happy all day long! Only five hundred shells at the Harbor Shop. Hurry, before they are all gone!" How many colors does it come in? Five. It glows in the dark. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. We can check it in a dark room. You will be happy all day long. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Pip says, Ads want to sell things, so they use big, happy words. Look for the facts first. Then decide for yourself. Now, phonics. Audible. Responsible. Aud and respons are not words by themselves, so they usually take ible. Debatable. Debate, drop the e, plus able. Questionable. Question plus able. Is it the best toy ever? That's debatable! Be smart shoppers, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, "This is the best toy ever!" Is it a fact? Today is a big day. Pip asks us to be the Fact Check Team for The Lighthouse News. All the island animals come to the newsroom to listen. Haru goes first. Puffins can dive under the water. That's a fact. We checked it in a book. Say it with me. That's a fact. We checked it in a book. Wonderful! Gus raises his wing. How did you check it? Kiko answers, We asked Captain Pell, and we read a book in the lighthouse library. lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, That's a fact. We checked it in a book. Five lenses are shining, and Captain Pell has an idea. Let's practice for the big discussion show! We go back to the round meeting room and sit in a circle. Riko is the chair today. She says, Today's topic is homework. Should we have homework on weekends? Say it with me. Should we have homework on weekends? Nice! Riko says, Let's hear from everyone. Haru raises his hand. I think we should, because practice makes us better. Kiko says, I see your point, but we need time to rest. Birimo says, I partly agree with both of you! Pip writes everything down. Let's read two posts from The Lighthouse News. "Readers' Voices. Gus writes: I think we should have a little homework on weekends. One reason is that we remember new things better. For example, I practice spelling for ten minutes every Saturday. Now I make fewer mistakes. Gale writes: I see my brother's point, but I don't think we need weekend homework. Weekends are for rest, family, and playing outside. Our brains need a break, too. Then we can learn more on Monday!" Who wants homework on weekends? Gus. Gus practices spelling for ten minutes every Saturday. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Our brains need a break. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Riko says, Both ideas are good. We don't have to choose today. Listening to both sides is the most important part. Now, phonics. Inspect. Spect means look. Predictable. Dict means say. I strongly believe it. Make STRONGLY big! Wait for me. For is soft. Responsible. Ible at the end. Great discussion, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Should we have homework on weekends? Today, we have another mini discussion. Anchor, Captain Pell's old dog, comes into the meeting room. He lies down by the window and wags his tail. That gives Haru an idea for a topic. Should our school have a class pet? Say it with me. Should our school have a class pet? Great! Riko says, I think so. We can learn to be responsible. Kiko says, I'm not sure about that. Caring for a pet is hard. Birimo asks, What do you mean by hard? Kiko answers, A pet needs care every day, even on holidays. Haru says, Let's get some facts. Captain Pell knows a lot about caring for a pet. So he gives us a card about Anchor. Let's read it. "Caring for Anchor. Anchor eats two meals a day, one in the morning and one in the evening. He needs fresh water all the time. We walk on the rocks every morning and every evening, even in the rain. He visits the animal doctor two times a year. Anchor is old now, so he sleeps a lot. A pet needs care every day, even on holidays. In my opinion, caring for a pet is hard work, but it is full of love. Captain Pell" How many meals does Anchor eat a day? Two. Caring for a pet is hard work, but it is full of love. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Anchor visits the animal doctor two times a year. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Riko and Kiko smile. Both ideas are good, and now we have more facts. Now, phonics. Spectacular. Spect means look. Verdict. Dict means say. I love this idea. Say LOVE strongly. I can help you. Can is short and soft. Suitable. Suit plus able. Let's take good care of each other!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, Should our school have a class pet? Today, Pip needs help again. The last page of The Lighthouse News is empty. Pip says, Please write opinion paragraphs for my readers! I explain the steps. First, write your opinion. Then, give two reasons. Riko writes first. I think we should read every day. First, it's fun. Second, we learn new words. So, let's read together! Say it with me. I think we should read every day. First, it's fun. Second, we learn new words. So, let's read together! Beautiful! Kiko asks, How should I end it? Riko says, Say your opinion again. It makes the paragraph strong. Riko adds more details, and her paragraph grows to about sixty words. Let's read it. "My Opinion, by Riko. I think we should read every day. First, it's fun. Books take us to new places, like dragon islands and snowy mountains. Second, we learn new words. For example, I learned the word spectacular in a story about the sea. Even ten minutes a day can help. So, let's read together! Reading every day makes our minds strong and happy." What are Riko's two reasons? Reading is fun, and we learn new words. What is her example? She learned the word spectacular. Riko learned the word spectacular in a story. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Reading makes our minds strong. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. Look at the shape of her paragraph. Opinion, reason one, reason two, and the opinion again. Now it's your turn. Birimo writes, I think we should eat cake every day. Everyone laughs. Now, phonics. Perspective. Spect means look. Dictation. Dict means say. That's exactly my point. Say EXACTLY strongly. Let's stop and think. And is tiny. Reasonable. Reason plus able. Happy writing, everyone!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I think we should read every day. First, it's fun. Second, we learn new words. So, let's read together! Today, Captain Pell gives us a goodbye tour of the lighthouse. Anchor walks next to him, slowly and happily. Haru says, Let's go to the lamp room first! The view is amazing. Kiko says, I see your point, but I have a different idea. Say it with me. I see your point, but I have a different idea. Very polite! Kiko says, Let's start at the library on the first floor. Then we can walk up, one floor at a time. Riko checks. So you mean we should visit the library first? Kiko says, Yes, that's right. Haru smiles. You are so right. That's a good plan. Captain Pell gives us a tour card. Let's read it. "Goodbye Tour of the Lighthouse of Ideas. Stop one: the Library. Here, you shared opinions and said, I agree with you. Stop two: the Round Meeting Room. Here, you listened to everyone and decided together. Stop three: Pip's Newsroom. Here, you sorted facts and opinions and checked the news. Stop four: the Lamp Room. Five lenses are shining, and one lens is still dark. Tomorrow is the big discussion show. I'm sure the last lens will shine! Captain Pell" Where did we sort facts and opinions? In Pip's newsroom. How many lenses are shining? Five. I'm sure the last lens will shine. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's an opinion. It's Captain Pell's hope! At the end of the tour, we all say, Thank you for the tour, Captain Pell! Now, phonics. Respectful. Spect means look. Contradict. Dict means say. You are so right. Say SO strongly. I'd like to say something. To is short and soft. Visible. Ible at the end. See you at the big show!

lessons.teacherScript: Hello, everyone! Last time, we said, I see your point, but I have a different idea. Today is the World 29 Discussion Show! All the island animals sit in the round meeting room. Gus and Gale are in the front row, and Anchor sleeps by the door. Riko is the chair. Today's topic is a thank-you gift for Captain Pell. What do you think? Haru wants to sing a song for him. Kiko has a different idea, a painting of Anchor. Birimo wants a cake, of course! Everyone listens and gives reasons. Then they vote. Most people choose the painting. Suddenly, the lamp room fills with light. The sixth lens is shining! Captain Pell says, Sharing ideas makes the light brighter! Say it with me. Sharing ideas makes the light brighter! Fantastic! We say, Thank you, Captain Pell! Thank you, Anchor! Pip writes a special story. Let's read it. "The Lighthouse News, Special Edition. Tonight, the lighthouse was full of voices. At the World 29 Discussion Show, four friends talked about a thank-you gift for Captain Pell. Haru wanted a song. Kiko wanted a painting. Riko asked everyone for their opinions. Birimo said, Can I say something? Then he asked for cake. In the end, they voted for a painting of Anchor. Then all six lenses began to shine! The light reached far across the sea of clouds. By Pip" What did they vote for? A painting of Anchor. All six lenses are shining. Is this a fact or an opinion? It's a fact. Look! The beam reaches far away. What's that city? It's the City of Tomorrow! Now, phonics. Spectrum. Spect means look. Prediction. Dict means say. I really think so. Say REALLY strongly. We can do it together. Can is soft. Incredible. Agreeable. Ible and able. See you in the City of Tomorrow!
